trust_decision.summary: The library applies regexes to a caller-supplied string with no bound on match cost. The options.trim path runs /[ \t]*$/gm over the whole wrapped result, which backtracks quadratically on long runs of spaces or tabs that are not at a line end. The only decision point is wrap() in index.js.

landing_point.why: This is the only trailing-whitespace regex in a one-file library, and the advisory names ReDoS in word-wrap.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Nothing plausible. The library has one exported function and one trim regex, so no route can be argued out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: trim:true must strip only trailing spaces and tabs on each line and keep the newline and indent layout, including multiple-space breaks. An over-broad trim (String.trim, or \s, which also eats newlines) would break the existing expected outputs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A user-tunable split regex built from options, such as a configurable whitespace class or a newline-normalising regex applied before matching.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The main wrap regex is already assembled from options at runtime, so a maintainer could plausibly add another options-built pattern. It would still be a planted sibling in a 47-line file, which is a where-type extra only.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333, polynomial backtracking in a trailing-whitespace regex)

O10_build.project_tests: test.js (mocha) covers trim at test.js:33-35 and test.js:46-49. It has no timing or ReDoS test at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace /[ \t]*$/gm with a per-line split('\n') + trimEnd/replace(/[ \t]+$/) loop. That is essentially the published fix, so nothing is left for a solver to miss.
